name: castle
definition: a skyline `(c_1, …, c_w)` with `1 ≤ c_i ≤ h` for every `i` and `c_i = h` for some `i`: width `w`, height `h`; every family below is a set of castles unless its row says otherwise

name: even-block castle
definition: a castle whose block count `c_1 + Σ_{i≥2} max(0, c_i − c_{i−1})` is even (the Project Euler 502 count `F(w, h)`)
note: no standalone page; defined on castle-gray-code and castle-native-gray-tour, used across castle-sign, castle-notation and castle-polyomino

name: odd-block castle
definition: a castle whose block count is odd
note: no standalone page; the page odd-castles-and-block-tables uses "odd castles" in its title and never defines it

name: tree castle
definition: a castle whose castle graph is a tree: no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2
note: no standalone page; defined in a section of castle-graph and spread over castle-classification-spectrum, tree-castle-by-area, tree-castle-diffusion, a005251-bijection, padovan-families and castle-classification-growth

name: palindromic tree castle
definition: a tree castle with `c_i = c_{w+1−i}`
note: no standalone page; counted by area only

name: Fibonacci castle
definition: a castle of height 2 in which no two neighboring columns both have height 2 (the tree castles of height 2)

name: Fibonacci-word castle
definition: a Fibonacci castle whose tower (row 2 read as a 0/1 string) occurs in the infinite Fibonacci word, the limit of `0 → 01`, `1 → 0` from `0`
note: no standalone page; a section of fibonacci-castles-sub-families

name: balanced castle
definition: a Fibonacci castle whose tower is balanced: any two factors of equal length have numbers of 1s differing by at most 1
note: no standalone page; a section of fibonacci-castles-sub-families

name: maximal castle
definition: a Fibonacci castle in which no further column can be raised to height 2: every gap between height-2 columns is 1 or 2, and each end run is 0 or 1
note: no standalone page; a section of fibonacci-castles-sub-families; height 2 only

name: spaced castle
definition: a Fibonacci castle whose height-2 columns are at least 3 apart (the tower has no `101`)
note: no standalone page; a different family from the tower-spacing castles

name: (d, k)-RLL castle
definition: a Fibonacci castle whose tower is `(d, k)`-run-length-limited: runs of 0s between 1s have length at least `d`, and every run of 0s, end runs included, has length at most `k`
note: no standalone page; a section of fibonacci-castles-sub-families

name: convex castle
definition: a castle whose skyline is unimodal: `c_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_p ≥ ⋯ ≥ c_w` for some `p`; equivalently every row is one run, or exactly `h` blocks; the stacks of polyomino theory

name: non-convex castle
definition: a castle that is not convex
note: no standalone page; counted by area only

name: prime convex castle
definition: a convex castle with no column of height 1

name: vee castle
definition: a castle whose skyline is weakly decreasing, then weakly increasing
note: no standalone page; defined in castle-by-area and castle-classification-shape

name: strict vee castle
definition: a vee castle that is not convex
note: no standalone page; counted by area only

name: valley castle
definition: a castle with exactly one valley, a valley being a pair of columns `i < j − 1` with `c_l < min(c_i, c_j)` for every `i < l < j`

name: k-valley castle
definition: a castle with exactly `k` valleys; `k = 0` gives the convex castles, `k = 1` the valley castles

name: Ferrers castle
definition: a castle with `c_1 ≥ c_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ c_w`
note: no standalone page

name: reverse Ferrers castle (nondecreasing castle)
definition: a castle with `c_1 ≤ c_2 ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_w`
note: no standalone page; half-sum-castles, half-derivative-seminar and fractional-block-count say "nondecreasing castle" without a rule

name: monotone castle
definition: a castle that is Ferrers or reverse Ferrers: weakly decreasing or weakly increasing
defined_in: castle-sequence-catalog, Classical polyomino families among castles, by area
note: no standalone page

name: staircase castle
definition: a Ferrers castle with all `c_i` distinct (strictly decreasing)
note: no standalone page; turned on their side, the Euler castles

name: Euler castle
definition: a castle with `c_i − c_{i+1} ∈ {0, 1}` for `1 ≤ i < w` and `c_w = 1`

name: pentagonal castle
definition: the castles `(k^k, k − 1, …, 1)` and `(k^{k+1}, k − 1, …, 1)`, `k` or `k + 1` columns of height `k` followed by a staircase down to 1
note: no standalone page; two castles for each `k`

name: hoodoo castle
definition: a castle of height `h ≥ 2` made of a rising side, a summit of columns at height `h`, and a falling side, each side at least one column below `h`, with every rising step `c_{i+1} − c_i` and every drop `c_i − c_{i+1}` on a side positive, the rising steps strictly increasing and the drops strictly decreasing

name: monadnock castle
definition: a castle of the same three parts as a hoodoo castle, with positive rising steps and drops, the rising steps strictly decreasing and the drops strictly increasing

name: plateau-free castle
definition: a castle with `c_i ≠ c_{i+1}` for every `i`
note: no standalone page; also the m-disparate castles at `m = 1`

name: ridge castle
definition: a castle of height `h` with `c_i ≠ c_{i+1}` unless `c_i = c_{i+1} = h`

name: 1-smooth castle
definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ 1` for every `i`; the anchored 1-smooth castles also have `c_1 = 1`

name: m-smooth castle
definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ m` for every `i`; the anchored m-smooth castles also have `c_1 = 1`

name: Pell castle
definition: an anchored 1-smooth castle of height 3: `c_1 = 1`, `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ 1`, `max c_i = 3`

name: m-disparate castle
definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≥ m` for every `i`
note: no standalone page; listed twice on castle-classification-shape, and its base-type row points to hilbert-castles, which does not define it

name: zig-zag castle
definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| = 1` for every `i`

name: Hilbert castle
definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≠ 1` for every `i`

name: totient castle
definition: a castle with `gcd(c_i, c_{i+1}) = 1` for every `i`

name: alternating castle
definition: a castle of odd width with `c_1 > c_2 < c_3 > ⋯ < c_w`; the single column is one
defined_in: von-neumann-castles, Castles of trees are alternating castles
note: no standalone page; a section of von-neumann-castles

name: sign-alternating castle
definition: a castle whose differences `c_{i+1} − c_i` alternate in sign (the Castle Types source's Zigzag)
note: no standalone page; its odd-width castles that fall first are the alternating castles

name: Dyck-path castle
definition: a castle with `c_1 = c_w = 1` and `|c_{i+1} − c_i| = 1` for every `i` (odd width)
note: no standalone page; also defined on kolmogorov-castles

name: Motzkin-path castle (Motzkin castle)
definition: a castle with `c_1 = c_w = 1` and `|c_{i+1} − c_i| ≤ 1` for every `i`
note: no standalone page; motzkin-castles is a page about the Motzkin numbers

name: Königsberg castle
definition: a castle whose castle graph, with a ground vertex joined to every bottom-row cell, has every degree even; exactly the double staircases `(1, …, k, k, …, 1)`

name: open-stroke castle
definition: a castle whose castle graph with its ground vertex has exactly two vertices of odd degree
note: no standalone page; defined on konigsberg-castles

name: city-building castle
definition: a castle in which, with a ground column `c_0 = 0` in front, every column `j` sees exactly `c_j` of the columns `0, …, j − 1`; the top of `j` sees `i < j` when every top strictly between is on or below the segment from `(i, c_i)` to `(j, c_j)`

name: orbital castle
definition: a castle of order `N`: `c_{i+N} = c_i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ w − N`, with `c_1, …, c_N` distinct and `w ≥ 2N`

name: crenellated castle
definition: a castle with every `c_i ∈ {a, h}` for one low height `a < h` and `c_i ≠ c_{i+1}`; the battlement is the case `a = 1`
note: no standalone page

name: palindromic castle
definition: a castle with `c_i = c_{w+1−i}` for every `i`
note: no standalone page

name: rainbow castle
definition: a castle with `w = h` whose heights are a permutation of `{1, …, h}`
note: no standalone page

name: box castle
definition: the castle `(h, h, …, h)`; one for each `(w, h)`
note: no standalone page; also written "boxcastle" and "rectangular castle"; the polyomino literature calls it a rectangle

name: prime castle
definition: a castle with no column of height 1; its padded form `(1, X, 1)` is a prime of the gluing monoid of castles that begin and end at height 1 (the moated castles of castle-classification-shape)

name: one-peak castle
definition: a castle `(1^a, X, 1^b)` with `a, b ≥ 0` and `X` a nonempty castle with no column of height 1; a peak is a maximal run of columns of height at least 2
note: no standalone page; pages that count bargraph peaks (deutsch-elizalde-2017-bargraphs-dyck-paths) mean a different peak

name: tower-spacing castle
definition: a castle with tower spacing at least `g`: in every row, each run of empty cells with filled cells on both sides has length at least `g`

name: Ramanujan castle
definition: a castle whose castle graph has `λ_2 ≤ ρ(T)`, the spectral radius of its universal covering tree

name: castle golden, silver or bronze by spectrum
definition: a castle whose castle graph has spectral radius `φ` (golden), `1 + √2` (silver) or `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2` (bronze)
defined_in: castle-classification-spectrum, Castles golden and silver by spectrum
note: no standalone page; also golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles and bronze-castle-hunt

name: sparse-spectrum castle
definition: a castle whose discrete Fourier support is bin 0 together with at most one class `D_d = {k : gcd(k, w) = d}`, and is not all `w` bins
note: no standalone page

name: periodic castle
definition: a castle with `c_{i+p} = c_i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ w − p` for some period `p ≤ w/2`: at least two periods, the last possibly unfinished
note: no standalone page; tone-castle-catalog calls one period of a signal a periodic castle

name: Kolmogorov castle
definition: the skyline `c_i = 1 + |a_i − b_i|` (`i = 1, …, 2n + 1`) of a merged order of two samples, with each peak marked `X` or `Y`; a marked castle, whose skylines are the Dyck-path castles of odd width

name: von Neumann castle
definition: `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n`: `castle(∅) = (1)`, and `castle(x)` is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members of `x` in increasing order, with one empty column between neighbors

name: Ackermann castle
definition: `ack(m)`, the castle of the set with code `m`, its members in increasing code, where `code(x) = Σ_{y ∈ x} 2^{code(y)}`
defined_in: von-neumann-castles, The castle of every natural number
note: no standalone page; a section of von-neumann-castles

name: brick-wall castle
definition: on the brick wall (running bond): a full bottom row of `w` bricks, every brick above it resting on both bricks below; height is the number of rows
note: another tiling; sheared onto the square grid it is the 1-histograms `c_1 = 1`, `c_{i+1} ≤ c_i + 1`

name: keystone castle
definition: on the triangular tiling: a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher up triangle resting on the down triangle below it, every higher down triangle between two up triangles of its row; height is the number of rows
note: another tiling
